messages:
maria_support: FYI a customer (acme corp) is seeing sudden latency spikes and occasional 5xxs hitting /v1/generate. They are EU-based but traces show routing through us-west. Sample from their logs below — trace_id=ab12cd34ef56 and latency ~1150ms.

kevin_sre: can you paste the exact request headers and the raw log line? need x-request-id/trace id to pull the Jaeger trace.

maria_support: here's the log snippet: `ts=2026-03-15T14:12:03Z req_id=01F8Z7 trace_id=ab12cd34ef56 x-region=eu-west-1 x-client=acme-frontend status=200 latency=1150ms`
Customer also ran: `curl -i https://api.redwood.net/v1/generate` and got `x-redwood-region: us-west-2`. Jaeger link: https://jaeger.redwood.local/traces/ab12cd34ef56

kevin_sre: looking at trace... I can see an early 302 redirect from the edge LB to a us-west backend. Root span shows router decision: fallback policy invoked. I want to check LB/health-check events for eu cluster at that minute. Also, did the customer set any `Prefer-Region` header? if not, routing uses geo/health only.

oliver_ingest: pulled router logs for 2026-03-15T14:12Z: `router: route_match=eu-west-1 backend=api-us-west-2 session=sticky=false health=unhealthy probe=503` — the eu backend returned 503 to the probe so the router fell back. Found the routing policy in prod: 
```
route_policy:\n  prefer_region: eu-west-1\n  fallback: any\n  fallback_weight: 100\n```
That `fallback_weight: 100` will push 100% traffic to fallback when primary unhealthy. Too aggressive.

sarah_oncall: adding that DNS TTL was recently lowered to 5s in a deploy (to speed rollouts) — that makes clients more likely to get a different endpoint during flapping. Repro steps I used locally:
1) scale down eu app: `kubectl -n prod scale deploy/api --replicas=0` (simulates health failure)
2) `curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood.net" http://lb-eu.redwood.net/v1/generate`
Response: `HTTP/1.1 302 Found` with `Location: https://api.redwood.net.us-west-2/v1/generate` and header `x-redwood-region: us-west-2`. So client follows redirect and you hit us-west.

maria_support: this is odd — the customer is on a dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in eu. Why would fallback be allowed for a reserved tenant? they should be isolated.

kevin_sre: spotted the cause: autoscaler misbehavior. The reserved pool had a label mismatch during a maintenance reconcile (`team: redwood-prod` vs expected `team: redwood`) so the autoscaler thought there were 0 endpoints and scaled the instance group down. Health probes then saw no endpoints and marked the eu backend unhealthy. That triggered the fallback routing. Opening a hotfix to make the autoscaler ignore reserved/dedicated pools unless explicitly targeted.

oliver_ingest: created quick config change: set `fallback_weight: 10` (was 100) and revert DNS TTL to 60s. Also added a router safeguard to never fallback for `tenant_type: reserved`. PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routers/pull/4567

deploy-bot: deployment started: pr=4567 env=prod target=routers region=eu-west-1

sarah_oncall: monitoring update: p95 latency for eu tenants dropped from ~1.2s to ~160ms after the rollout; I don't see cross-region traces in the last 15m :thumbsup:

maria_support: I will send ACME the RCA: autoscaler label mismatch caused reserved pool to scale to zero -> health probes failed -> routing fallback (fallback_weight too high) -> cross-region redirect -> higher latency. Mitigations: hotfix to autoscaler, lower fallback_weight, increase DNS TTL. Thanks team!
